records.title: Bell Warden glossary
records.body:
# Bell Warden glossary

- **Slack bell**: rung at slack water.
- **Tally stick**: a record of unpaid crossings.

records.title: Chapter 4 — Tide Mill
records.body:
# Tide Mill

The mill wheel turned only when the sea allowed it.

records.title: Chapter 1 — Low Water
records.body:
The harbour emptied at low water, as it did twice a day — once for the tide, once for the tax.

“Eleven rings,” Ivo Marsh said.  
Nobody on the quay answered; even Renée kept her eyes on the bells.

records.title: Chapter 2 — The Bell Tax
records.body: The wardens came at slack tide with their tally sticks.

records.title: Chapter 3 — Salt Road
records.body: Salt road ran inland from the mill, white as a ledger page.

records.title: Bell tax
records.body: Is the bell tax collected daily or at each slack tide?

records.title: Bell tax — settled
records.body: The wardens collect the bell tax at every slack tide.

records.title: Ivo Marsh
records.body: Harbour clerk. Forty-one. Counts the mooring rings every morning.

records.title: Ring count
records.body: Keep the ring count at eleven in every later chapter.

records.title: Outline — Part One
records.body:
1. Low water.
2. The bell tax.
3. Salt road.

records.title: The empty quay
records.body: Ivo counted the mooring rings. Eleven, again.

records.title: A warden at the door
records.body: The warden’s lantern was out, which meant nothing good.

records.title: Tally sticks
records.body: Each notch was a crossing nobody paid for.

records.title: Discarded bell theory
records.body: The bells were never rung at all.

records.title: The Bell Wardens
records.body: Wardens ring the harbour bells at slack water and collect the bell tax.
